title: Canonical and unrestricted observations in a finite checkerboard gradient model
abstract: We compare unrestricted observations and canonical original-channel rectangle means for a finite two-channel source-weighted checkerboard gradient form. Exact orthogonal restoring ranks and a fixed-positive-angle order-n Fourier construction are retained. We add a constructive every-window corner-matching obstruction for a three-dimensional cyclic product-slice extension. Its nonwrapping product-slice restrictions yield logarithmic necessary counts for fixed or bounded-motion cuts. A rapidly moving cyclic24n-row family fails through a short four-step resonance. Its wrapped complements are not nonwrapping canonical cells, so that failure is not transferred merely by refining means. A separate new cutoff covers the additional chart-boundary corners and constructs a real nonzero actual-coexact field annihilating each of36n-24 nonwrapping refined means, with Q<7c||z||^2/16 at an enormous stated finite threshold. Original counting normalization, source parity, coexact membership, exact zeros and nonzero norm are derived explicitly. The general canonical coexact O(n)-versus-logarithm question remains open. Historical originality and wider quantitative relevance are unestablished; no physical Yang-Mills gap or continuum result follows.
